candidate_datasets.name: The Reptile Database
candidate_datasets.role: viper reproductive biology

obstacles: The groups include multiple reproductive modes.
rationale: Reproductive mode is directly recorded in established public species resources. Their coverage is adequate to characterize the main patterns and identify decisive exceptions.

operationalization: Compare eggshell structure, thermal physiology, and egg retention across cartilaginous fishes and vipers. Soft internal egg coverings and an association between lower developmental temperature and retention support components, but do not by themselves establish cold nature as the cause.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive mode and environmental data for cartilaginous fishes

candidate_datasets.name: The Reptile Database
candidate_datasets.role: viper reproduction and taxonomy

obstacles: Cold nature lacks a unique modern physiological definition.
Phylogeny and many ecological variables confound egg retention.
rationale: Observable predictions about egg covering and retention can be assessed from existing records. The claimed thermal cause is underspecified and difficult to distinguish from alternative evolutionary explanations.

operationalization: Determine testis position and scrotal anatomy in elephants and hedgehogs, then compare skin properties with related mammals having external testes. Internal position is directly testable, while support for skin unsuitability would require a specified biomechanical threshold.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: elephant and hedgehog pelvic and reproductive anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: species anatomy and reproductive descriptions

obstacles: Skin suitability is undefined.
Two taxa cannot separate skin properties from ancestry and developmental history.
rationale: Public anatomy can settle where the testes lie in both named animals. It cannot cleanly test the proposed causal reason without adding a novel biomechanical operationalization.

operationalization: Code body orientation, mouth contact, arm entwinement, and genital contact from identified mating videos of octopuses, cuttlefish, and squid. Species mating without the stated configuration refute the universal form.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: cephalopod reproductive-behavior accounts

candidate_datasets.name: Global Biotic Interactions
candidate_datasets.role: public reproductive interaction records

obstacles: Mating videos are sparse and biased toward accessible species.
Mouth to mouth may describe body orientation rather than literal oral contact.
rationale: The posture has clear observable components and can be assessed in existing footage and reports. Taxonomic coverage is too uneven to resolve all cephalopods without substantial additional observations.

operationalization: Trace the hectocotylized arm's anatomy, spermatophore transport, and insertion during octopus mating. Connection to sperm transfer or experimental association with fertilization refutes the assertion that it is only for attachment.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoSource
candidate_datasets.role: cephalopod reproductive and arm anatomy

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: octopus reproductive biology and species accounts

obstacles: Detailed functional observations are concentrated in a subset of octopus species.
rationale: The claim makes a direct functional-anatomical prediction about a named organ. Public anatomical and reproductive evidence is adequate to determine whether the arm transfers spermatophores and contributes to generation.

operationalization: Use parent-offspring genetic matches, recorded oviposition, and complete life-cycle observations for fleas, flies, and blister beetles. Repeated production from conspecific parents and failure of sterile putrefying material to generate insects refute spontaneous generation.

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: public insect DNA barcodes linking life stages and species

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Sequence Read Archive
candidate_datasets.role: open genomic and parentage-capable sequence data for insects

obstacles: Historical putrefaction terminology covers diverse substrates.
rationale: Parentage and life-cycle predictions are explicit and sharply discriminating. Extensive public genetic, developmental, and rearing evidence makes the claim resolvable without new data.

operationalization: Calculate female-to-male body-size ratios for sexed adult insect specimens across species, then estimate the fraction with female-biased dimorphism using species-level weighting. A fraction at or below one half refutes 'most.'

candidate_datasets.name: BOLD Systems
candidate_datasets.role: identified insect specimens, images, and sex metadata where available

candidate_datasets.name: Natural History Museum Data Portal
candidate_datasets.role: digitized sexed insect specimens

obstacles: Sex and body size are missing from many records.
Sampling is strongly biased among insect orders.
rationale: Sexual size dimorphism is directly measurable, and public specimen images support many taxa. Missing sex metadata and extreme taxonomic imbalance prevent a defensible estimate over all mating insects without major compilation.

operationalization: For a representative insect sample, record which sex inserts which genital structure during copulation and estimate the species-weighted majority pattern. A male-insertion majority would refute the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: MorphoBank
candidate_datasets.role: comparative insect genital morphology for selected clades

obstacles: Insertion direction is not a standard database trait.
Genital homologies and sex-role terminology vary greatly among insects.
rationale: The behavior is observable after a precise definition, but existing open resources contain only scattered clade-specific descriptions. Resolving 'most insects' requires a new standardized comparative compilation and likely new observations.

operationalization: In multigenerational pedigrees with genomic and phenotype data, identify traits absent in parents but shared with grandparents or earlier ancestors and test inheritance models. Recurrence is measurable, but 'nothing has come to them' must be translated into no direct non-genetic material rather than no inherited DNA.

candidate_datasets.name: 1000 Genomes Project
candidate_datasets.role: public human variation and pedigree-related genomic resources

candidate_datasets.name: European Variation Archive
candidate_datasets.role: open genotype and variant data across species

obstacles: Remote resemblance is subjective without a specified phenotype.
Few fully public datasets combine deep pedigrees, images, and genomes.
rationale: Mendelian segregation provides measurable skipped-generation recurrence, and public genomic resources test mechanisms. The broad resemblance wording and lack of deep linked phenotypes limit direct resolution of the claim as phrased.

operationalization: Compare congenital morphology in offspring of parents with documented acquired amputations or injuries, separating inherited variants from acquired lesions. Any intact offspring establishes the existential 'not always' claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Animals
candidate_datasets.role: public inherited-trait records distinguishing genetic defects from acquired injuries

candidate_datasets.name: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man
candidate_datasets.role: public catalog of inherited human phenotypes and mechanisms

obstacles: Acquired parental injuries are rarely linked to offspring in open structured data.
rationale: The 'not always' quantifier requires only well-documented intact offspring and is highly discriminating. Public inheritance records and literature can resolve examples, though systematic parent-injury linkage is sparse.

operationalization: Trace the cellular origin and molecular composition of sperm using lineage, transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolic data, and compare it with a model in which every somatic part directly contributes material. Germline-restricted production with selective molecular inputs supports the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Human Protein Atlas
candidate_datasets.role: open tissue and testis-specific expression data

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public germ-cell and somatic-cell expression datasets

obstacles: Drawn from every part can mean direct tissue particles or metabolically derived nutrients.
rationale: Modern germline and molecular data directly distinguish pangenesis-like bodily contributions from localized gametogenesis. Public omics coverage is extensive, although the historical phrase requires a stated mechanistic interpretation.

operationalization: Model offspring number per reproductive event or year against adult body mass across animals, with reproductive mode and phylogeny controlled. A broadly negative relationship supports the tendency; no relationship or a positive one refutes it under a prespecified scope.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: body mass and reproductive output across animal species

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: fish size and fecundity records

obstacles: Few young can mean clutch size, annual output, or lifetime reproduction.
Reproductive mode and phylogeny are major confounders.
rationale: Body size and fecundity are standard, broadly available traits. A preregistered comparative model can resolve the general association now, though conclusions depend on the chosen reproductive-output definition.

operationalization: Estimate sex-specific height curves and compare height gained from birth to age five with gain from age five to adult height. Equality supports the stated half-versus-half partition, while a materially different ratio refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: NHANES
candidate_datasets.role: public age- and sex-specific human stature data

candidate_datasets.name: CDC Growth Charts
candidate_datasets.role: public reference height curves from childhood through adolescence

obstacles: The baseline for height gained may be birth length or zero.
Cross-sectional growth curves are not individual longitudinal trajectories.
rationale: Human stature by age is exceptionally well covered in open national data. Once the growth baseline and adult age are specified, standard curve estimation decisively tests the numerical claim.

operationalization: Relate adiposity measures to time-to-pregnancy, sperm quality, and live birth in men and women while controlling age, disease, and socioeconomic factors. The fertility association is testable, but conversion of reproductive secretion into fat would require a distinct metabolic mechanism and tracer evidence.

candidate_datasets.name: Demographic and Health Surveys
candidate_datasets.role: public-use fertility histories and anthropometric variables

candidate_datasets.name: NHANES
candidate_datasets.role: public adiposity, reproductive-health, and hormone variables

obstacles: Observational fertility is confounded by behavior and health.
The proposed conversion of secretion into fat is not a modern measurable pathway as stated.
rationale: Large public human datasets can test whether adiposity is associated with reduced fertility in both sexes. They cannot discriminate Aristotle's metabolic explanation from hormonal, behavioral, and clinical alternatives.

operationalization: Semen composition and biosynthetic precursors can be measured, but useful nutriment, final stage, secretion, and waste-product are evaluative categories that do not define mutually exclusive measurable alternatives.
obstacles: Useful versus waste is function-relative rather than a compositional dichotomy.
Final-stage nutriment lacks a modern biochemical criterion.
rationale: Public metabolomic and proteomic data could describe semen, but any composition could be redescribed as processed nutrient or bodily residue. The stated categories therefore do not yield a discriminating dataset test.

operationalization: Estimate age distributions for first ejaculation or sperm production and menarche, alongside voice change and breast stage, in comparable populations. Similar central ages within a prespecified tolerance support synchrony; separated distributions refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: NHANES
candidate_datasets.role: public puberty, reproductive-history, and examination data

candidate_datasets.name: Dataverse
candidate_datasets.role: repository for open population puberty datasets

obstacles: First semen production is less often recorded than menarche.
Puberty timing varies by population and secular period.
rationale: Pubertal milestones are standard epidemiological variables with substantial public data. Male onset is less precisely observed, but available cohorts can resolve whether the milestones occur at comparable ages in defined populations.

operationalization: Quantify sex differences in adult body mass across viviparous species and code menstruation or endometrial shedding. Existing data can test the size generalization and whether menstruation is unique to the class, but not infer that menstrual loss causes smaller size without stronger causal evidence.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: sex-linked mammalian body-size and life-history data

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive physiology and sexual dimorphism accounts

obstacles: Sexual size dimorphism varies in direction among mammals.
Most mammals do not menstruate in the human sense.
Causal inference is confounded by selection and life history.
rationale: Public comparative traits can strongly test the descriptive assertions and expose exceptions. They do not isolate menstrual discharge as the cause of body-size dimorphism, so the full explanation remains unresolved.

operationalization: Female reproductive physiology can be measured, but defining femaleness as male impotence and inability to concoct nutriment into semen makes the conclusion depend on Aristotelian categories rather than a distinct observation.
obstacles: Impotent male is a definitional analogy.
Concoction of final nutriment has no measurable modern criterion.
rationale: Gamete development data cannot decide whether the female is conceptually a deficient male. The formulation supplies no outcome that distinguishes it from non-hierarchical accounts of sex differentiation.

operationalization: Code overt cyclical uterine bleeding across placental mammals, distinguishing menstruation from estrous resorption and pathological bleeding. Any directly viviparous species without menstrual discharge refutes the universal claim, while flow measurements test the human abundance comparison.

candidate_datasets.name: Animal Diversity Web
candidate_datasets.role: mammalian reproductive-cycle accounts

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: aggregated mammalian reproductive traits and literature

obstacles: Menstruation and estrous bleeding are often conflated.
No single open database comprehensively codes endometrial shedding.
rationale: Reproductive physiology literature contains decisive evidence and counterexamples across mammals. Structured coverage and comparable discharge quantities are incomplete, so existing data resolve the universal qualitatively but not every abundance component.

operationalization: Map two fingers' breadth to a preregistered breast projection or Tanner stage and estimate menarche timing relative to that stage in longitudinal puberty cohorts. Concentration of menarche near the mapped threshold would support the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: NHANES
candidate_datasets.role: public menarche and adolescent development variables

candidate_datasets.name: Dataverse
candidate_datasets.role: repository search for open longitudinal puberty cohorts

obstacles: Two fingers' breadth is not a standardized breast measure.
Public data rarely pair frequent breast staging with exact menarche date.
rationale: Menarche data are abundant, but the proposed breast threshold needs substantial interpretation and linked longitudinal staging is limited. Existing cohorts can test a proxy, not the statement at its original measurement precision.

operationalization: Identify paternally inherited DNA and sperm-derived cellular material in embryos using phased parent-offspring genomes and embryology data. Reproducible paternal material physically present in embryos refutes the assertion that the male contributes only motion and form.

candidate_datasets.name: 1000 Genomes Project
candidate_datasets.role: public phased human inheritance data

candidate_datasets.name: European Nucleotide Archive
candidate_datasets.role: open parent-offspring and developmental sequence data across animals

obstacles: Form could be reinterpreted to include genetic information, but the no-material clause remains explicit.
rationale: Paternal alleles and sperm-derived structures are directly measurable material contributions. Massive public genomic and developmental datasets provide a decisive, non-circular test.

operationalization: Mate hens at known times during follicle and egg formation, then assay fertilization and embryo development for eggs whose albumen deposition had or had not begun. Fertility acquired after the stated developmental boundary would refute the timing claim.

candidate_datasets.name: Chicken QTLdb
candidate_datasets.role: public chicken reproductive genetics, but not the required timed insemination outcome

obstacles: No known open dataset links exact egg-formation stage at mating to subsequent fertility.
The whitening boundary needs modern oviduct-stage mapping.
rationale: The experiment and outcome are clear, but existing genetic and production databases do not record the required fine-grained timing. A controlled timed-mating study or release of equivalent archival records is needed.

operationalization: Sequentially mate hens to genetically distinguishable cocks at known follicle stages, genotype every chick, and quantify phenotype resemblance. Exclusive second-cock paternity and resemblance would support the claim; mixed or first-cock paternity would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: European Nucleotide Archive
candidate_datasets.role: public chicken genomic markers suitable for paternity, but not the required mating experiment

obstacles: No known open sequential-mating dataset records follicle stage and complete-brood paternity.
Resemblance must be replaced by genotype or specified traits.
rationale: Modern genotyping makes the claim highly testable, but generic chicken sequence data cannot supply the required sequential mating histories. New controlled data are needed for the exact stage-specific assertion.

operationalization: For externally fertilizing fishes, relate egg contact with fluorescently labelled or genetically traceable sperm to fertilization and embryo development. Fertilization without sperm contact or failure despite adequate contact would refute the strict formulation.

candidate_datasets.name: FishBase
candidate_datasets.role: reproductive modes and spawning biology of fishes

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open fish fertilization and sperm-performance datasets

obstacles: Sperm can disperse microscopically beyond visible milt.
The claim applies only to externally fertilizing oviparous fishes.
rationale: Sperm-egg contact and fertilization are standard experimental variables with extensive published and open data. Existing datasets and literature can test the mechanism across representative externally fertilizing species.

operationalization: Code locomotion and sexual system across animals, including simultaneous and sequential hermaphrodites. A mobile hermaphroditic species is a decisive counterexample to universal separation of sexes.

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: sexual systems and mobility of marine animals

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: aggregated reproductive and lifestyle traits

obstacles: Can move about requires a threshold for slow or life-stage-specific movement.
rationale: Mobility and hermaphroditism are well-documented traits, and a universal statement is resolved by public counterexamples. Existing marine and terrestrial species accounts provide ample discriminating evidence.

operationalization: Species persistence and extinction can be measured over finite intervals, but no finite dataset can establish eternity or that generation occurs for the purpose of species eternity.
obstacles: Eternal species is not finitely observable.
The purpose assigned to generation has no distinct prediction.
rationale: Fossil and phylogenetic data show finite lineage durations but cannot test metaphysical eternity or reproductive purpose. The same observations fit many non-teleological evolutionary accounts.

operationalization: Compare adult body mass or volume between vertebrates and invertebrates and between motile and sessile animals using species-level and phylogenetically weighted summaries. Reversed central tendencies refute either generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge: The Animal Ageing and Longevity Database
candidate_datasets.role: vertebrate and selected invertebrate body mass

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: size and lifestyle traits for marine invertebrates

obstacles: Bloodless only approximately maps to invertebrates.
Body size data underrepresent microscopic and sessile species.
Species weighting strongly affects the result.
rationale: Large open trait databases permit direct comparative tests of broad size tendencies. Coverage of small invertebrates and sessile taxa is biased, so the all-animal scope is only partially represented.

operationalization: Measure egg diameter or volume from laying through early development in birds, oviparous reptiles, fishes, crustaceans, and cephalopods. Post-laying growth in the latter groups and stable size in the former support the contrast; counter-patterns refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Dryad
candidate_datasets.role: open developmental and egg-size time-series datasets

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: egg and reproductive descriptions for marine animals

obstacles: Repeated egg-volume measurements are scattered rather than globally standardized.
Water uptake and embryo growth need separate definitions.
rationale: Egg size through development is directly measurable and existing studies cover examples in every named group. Sparse, heterogeneous time series prevent a comprehensive test of the universal class-level contrast.

operationalization: Map sanguineous to animals with Aristotle-recognizable blood and code viviparity, oviparity, and infertility across taxa. Viviparous invertebrates or blood-bearing animals with neither reproductive mode provide counterexamples under explicit definitions.

candidate_datasets.name: Encyclopedia of Life
candidate_datasets.role: aggregated reproductive-mode and taxonomic traits

candidate_datasets.name: SeaLifeBase
candidate_datasets.role: viviparity and oviparity records for fishes and marine invertebrates

obstacles: Sanguineous does not map exactly to a modern taxonomic or circulatory category.
Some animals use brooding or asexual modes outside the dichotomy.
rationale: Reproductive modes are broadly documented and can test the empirical pattern within a chosen mapping. Ambiguity in blood and the exhaustive viviparous-or-oviparous classification limits resolution of the claim exactly as stated.
